properties.name: The build profile is worth 2.2x on loop_status, and the live store carries 7.4x the bytes of its own content — two separate costs, and today's earlier numbers named neither
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-24 after Anthony pointed out that RocksDB compiles with assertions on unless DEBUG_LEVEL=0. He was right that it matters, and checking it found a second thing nobody was looking for.

⭐ WHAT PROMPTED IT: every performance number recorded EARLIER THE SAME DAY — including the 22.6s for `loop_status` that `dec:the-stop-hook-asks-the-graph-asynchronously` rests on — was taken against `target/debug/reflow2-mcp`, and NONE of them said so. A prior session had been careful about exactly this (`fact:the-orientation-reads-cost-ten-seconds-and-the-store-is-not-why` states 'MEASURED on real RocksDB with a RELEASE binary'), so the project already knew it mattered.

═══ THE CONTROLLED COMPARISON ═══

Both binaries built from the SAME commit the same afternoon (debug 14:02, release 14:21). Both read the SAME freshly-imported store, seeded once. Profile is the only variable:

    call            release   debug    ratio
    loop_status       4.5s     9.9s     2.2x
    detect_gaps      0.98s     1.97s    2.0x
    claim_report     0.00s     0.00s      --

⇒ **THE BUILD PROFILE IS WORTH ABOUT 2.2x ON THIS CALL.** Real, and users run the release binary while every number quoted today came from debug.

═══ 🛑 AND THE BIGGER SURPRISE, WHICH IS NOT THE PROFILE ═══

Both of those are FAR below the 22.6s measured this morning. That gap must not be attributed to the profile, because THREE things differ between the two measurements and only one was controlled:

  1. BUILD PROFILE — measured: 2.2x.
  2. STORE PHYSICAL STATE — the live store is **89 MB across 25 SST files**; a fresh store holding the SAME 3,111 nodes from the same export is **12 MB with 0 SSTs**. Identical logical content, **7.4x the bytes**, from months of accumulated overwrites and uncompacted levels.
  3. TRANSPORT — this morning went over the shared HTTP daemon; this went over stdio, direct.

⚠️ **(2) IS A SIZE MEASUREMENT, NOT A LATENCY ONE.** 7.4x the bytes is correlated with the slowdown and is a plausible cause; nothing here proves it drives the latency. Saying it does would be the same error this project has already paid for once — two numbers agreeing is not causation, and that lesson was recorded THIS MORNING.

═══ WHAT SURVIVES, AND WHAT NEEDS QUALIFYING ═══

✅ `dec:the-stop-hook-asks-the-graph-asynchronously` STANDS. Even at the most favourable figure here — 4.5s, release binary, fresh store, direct transport — a Stop hook that blocks that long is unacceptable, and the path the hook actually runs on is demonstrably slower than that.

🛑 BUT ITS STATED NUMBER IS UNDER-QUALIFIED. '22.6s, repeatably' is TRUE as measured — live graph, shared HTTP daemon, debug binary — and reads as a property of the call. **A number is a measurement of a whole setup, not of the code**, and a later reader comparing it against a release build on a fresh store will conclude the earlier work was wrong when it was only differently situated.

═══ ⭐ THE LEAD WORTH FOLLOWING, and it is cheaper than anything discussed today ═══

If the store's physical state does drive the latency, a COMPACTION of the live store is a far cheaper win than any code change considered today — and nothing in reflow2 currently reports that its own store has grown to several times the size of its content. That is unmeasured and is stated here as a lead rather than a finding.
